newsitem.title: CANADA: CWB may export up to 3 mln T malt barley in 96/97.
newsitem.headline: CWB may export up to 3 mln T malt barley in 96/97.

text.p: The Canadian Wheat Board may export a record 3.0 million tonnes of malting barley in marketing year 1996/97 (Aug/July), the CWB's head said.

"The malting barley pool (export account) this past year is probably going to come in at around 2.4 million tonnes and I think we can work that up to 3.0 million tonnes if we get the quality for this year," the CWB's Lorne Hehn said.
The CWB exported 1.06 million tonnes of malting barley in 1994/95 and 2.36 million tonnes of malting barley in 1993/94.
"If this (warm) weather continues we'll have ample quantities," Hehn said.
Sixty to 70 varieties of barley grown on Canada's Prairies can be used to extract malt for making beer as well as be fed to livestock.

Prairie farmers began harvesting what could be a record barley crop of more than 15 million tonnes provided a killing frost does not strike too early in September, reducing production to feed quality.
Hehn declined to discuss feed barley export projections.

A spokesman for Canada's Agriculture Minister, Ralph Goodale said Goodale may decide next month how to act on a federal export review panel's suggestion that feed barley be taken out of the CWB's monopoly.
